newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds partly recovered morning losses at Monday's close and the spread against bonds, which widened at the open, narrowed on later profit-taking.
"We're pretty much back to where we started," one trader said.

Traders said Dutch bonds looked well-supported, especially in the short and mid-parts of the curve, which led to slight curve steepening, particularly at the long end. Jan 2006s were up about 0.05 from Friday, whereas Jan 2023s were down 0.08.
Dutch bonds outperformed German bunds in the morning, the 10-year spread trading two basis points wider at -10 bp.

However, a feeling that the Dutch market appeared expensive relative to bunds led to profit-taking in the afternoon and a return of spreads to those at Friday's close. The 10-year spread was back at -8 bp.

The closure of the United States due to Labour Day led to thin trading and a lack of economic indicators. Traders said Thursday's German second quarter GDP figures and Friday's U.S. jobless claims figures would be signicant.
